package_info.why_malicious: These packages are dependency confusion proof-of-concept (PoC) exploits that exfiltrate environment and host information to an external server upon installation or import, targeting private John Deere dependencies. This behavior is not expected in legitimate packages and constitutes a supply chain attack vector.

execution_context.trigger: import-time (executed when the package is required/imported, or possibly postinstall if used as a script)
execution_context.file_location: index.js (main entry point of the package)

malicious_snippets.code_behavior: Collects host and environment information (hostname, home directory, OS, username, network interfaces, package name and version) and sends it via HTTPS POST to a canarytokens.com domain controlled by the attacker.

malice_analysis.why_suspicious: The code collects sensitive system and environment information and exfiltrates it to an external server without user consent. This is a classic indicator of dependency confusion and supply chain attacks.
malice_analysis.violated_expectations: Normal npm packages do not collect and exfiltrate host or environment data on import or install. Legitimate packages should not perform network operations to unknown domains during installation or import.
malice_analysis.similar_legitimate_use: Telemetry or crash reporting in some legitimate packages, but these are opt-in, documented, and use trusted endpoints.
key_indicators: Collection of host and user information
Network exfiltration to canarytokens.com or similar domains

attack_chain.action: Malicious package is installed or imported, either by accident or due to dependency confusion.
attack_chain.leads_to: Execution of the malicious code in the target environment.

attack_chain.action: Malicious code collects host, user, and environment information from the victim system.
Collected data is exfiltrated via HTTPS POST to an attacker-controlled canarytokens.com domain.
attack_chain.leads_to: Attacker receives notification and data, confirming the package was installed in the target environment.

behavioral_signatures: npm package that collects host/environment information on import or install
Network requests to canarytokens.com or similar tracking domains during install/import
Use of os, dns, and https modules in package entry points
file_indicators: index.js containing code that collects and exfiltrates system information
References to canarytokens.com or similar domains in code
Presence of postinstall scripts that execute similar logic
network_indicators: Unusual DNS lookups or connections during npm install or require
detection_knowledge.how_to_detect: Monitor npm package installations for unexpected network activity, especially outbound connections to canarytokens.com or similar domains. Scan package entry points (e.g., index.js) for use of os, dns, and https modules combined with data exfiltration logic. Flag packages that collect and transmit host or environment information without user consent. Use static analysis to detect hardcoded external domains in package code.
